origin.description: Finds the split in the text left after controls are removed, then extracts each piece with substr_ctl.
origin.usage: strsplit_ctl(x, split, fixed = FALSE, perl = FALSE, useBytes = FALSE, warn = getOption("fansi.warn", TRUE), term.cap = getOption("fansi.term.cap", dflt_term_cap()), ctl = "all", normalize = getOption("fansi.normalize", FALSE), carry = getOption("fansi.carry", FALSE), terminate = getOption("fansi.terminate", TRUE))
origin.details: Finds the split in the text left after controls are removed, then extracts each piece with substr_ctl.
origin.value: A character vector, or a list of character vectors for strsplit.

translation.description: Finds the split in the text left after controls are removed, then extracts each piece with substr_ctl.
translation.usage: strsplit_ctl(x, split, fixed=False, perl=False, useBytes=False, warn=None, term_cap=None, ctl="all", normalize=None, carry=None, terminate=None)
translation.details: Finds the split in the text left after controls are removed, then extracts each piece with substr_ctl. A string is one element. None is a missing string. The replacement functions are substr_ctl_replace and substr2_ctl_replace.
translation.value: A list of strings, or a list of lists for strsplit.
